subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Great Western Railway was a railroad built between 1835 and 1841.
• It was the first broad-gauge railway in England.
• It connected the cities of London and Bristol.
• It was one hundred eighteen miles long.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the distance covered by the Great Western Railway. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The one-hundred-eighteen-mile-long Great Western Railway connected the English cities of London and Bristol.
choices.B: The Great Western Railway was the first broad-gauge railway in England.
choices.C: The Great Western Railway, which connected two English cities, was built between 1835 and 1841.
choices.D: A historic English railway, the Great Western Railway was completed in 1841.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes the distance covered by the Great Western Railway, noting that the railway, which connected the two English cities in its name, was one hundred eighteen miles long.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. While the sentence mentions that the railway connected two English cities, it doesn't emphasize the specific distance covered by the railway.
